history.period: Legendary origin in Dvapara Yuga; historically renovated in the 10th century AD; a 1516 AD copper-plate inscription records a land grant by the Kumbhala king
history.summary: Kanipura Sri Gopalakrishna Temple at Kumble (Kumbla), about 13 km north of Kasaragod town, is an ancient Vaishnavite shrine and one of the extant Abhimana Kshethrams. Legend holds that the Krishnashila idol of child Gopalakrishna, worshipped by Krishna's foster mother Yashoda, was gifted by Krishna himself to sage Kanva Maharshi, who installed it here (the name Kanipura derives from Kanvapura, after Kanva). Historical records state the temple was renovated in the 10th century by King Jayasimha of the Kadamba dynasty, whose capital was Kumbla and whose administration was conducted in the name of Kanipura Sri Gopalakrishna; the coronation of the Kumbla Rajas was solemnized at the temple's Vasantha Katte. The priests belong to the Kota Brahmin community. CSV town corrected: the temple is at Kumble, not Kasaragod town.

name: Kanipura Sri Gopalakrishna Temple
town_description: Kumble (Kumbla) is a coastal town in Kasaragod district of northern Kerala, about 13 km north of Kasaragod town on National Highway 66. It was the capital of the Kumbla (Kumbala) kingdom of the Kadamba dynasty, and ruins of the old fort still testify to its historical significance. The Kumbha Hole river flows past the temple and joins the Arabian Sea nearby.

travel.airport: Mangalore International Airport, about 47-48 km away (verify)
travel.railway: Kumbala railway station, about 650 m from the temple; Kasaragod station and Mangaluru junction also nearby
travel.road: On NH-66; regular buses from Kasaragod, Mangaluru and Kumbala; walkable from the Kumble bus stand

visitor_information.best_time: November to March; the annual festival in January (Makara Sankranti) is the major draw
